segments.title: Placeholder: queue refresher
segments.body:
A **queue** is first in, first out: you add to the back and take from the front, like a line at a till.

In Python, `collections.deque` is a queue: `append` adds to the back and `popleft` takes from the front.

segments.title: Placeholder: Python refresher
segments.body: A **dictionary** maps keys to values: `graph = {"A": ["B", "C"]}` stores the neighbours of `A` under the key `"A"`, and `graph["A"]` reads them back.

activities.title: Placeholder: which item leaves the queue?

config.prompt: The queue holds 3, 7, 2 (front first). Which item leaves first?

feedback.b: 2 joined last, so it leaves last: a queue is first in, first out.
feedback.c: 7 is in the middle. The front item leaves first.

feedback.b: `graph["A"]` reads the value stored under the key "A", not the key itself.
feedback.c: "A" is a key in the dictionary, so reading it works.
